Moscow was the most secure place to stay out of America's grasp, he knew this very well. He was a bit nervous, officially his asylum visa had expired last year but the intentions of the Russian governement had seeped trough that the status would be prolonged. With his passport taken by the USA it wasnt like he was going anywhere anyway. With his laptop in his lap he stared out of the window lost in thoughts.

A sudden knock on the door and two FSB safety agents wearing sunglasses entering the room. The agents nodded at Edward and made a quick sweep around the room. When they where finished one of them spoke into his mic. "комната безопасна . Большой медведь очищается , чтобы войти."

The door opened again and [the most powerful man in the world walked into the room](http://i.imgur.com/iSRgad2.gif). "Sorry to keep you waiting, also about your status, but my schedule.... is very busy as you can imagine! And I wanted to sort this out personally" Snowden nodded and swallowed, he had known he would have an important visitor today but hadn't dreamt of sitting across the Russian president this morning. The two men made some chit chat about the last few years and how Snowden was handling his stay in Russia. The tension and anxiety quickly evaporated once the talks continued and [lunch](http://www.lcbo.com/content/dam/lcbo/products/137117.jpg/jcr:content/renditions/cq5dam.web.1280.1280.jpeg) was served.

Our goals might not be the same but they are alligned so we can sympathise to that and would like to facilitate you in your crusade for truth and justice. We will offer you full freedom in your endavours and will respect your autonomy in this operation." Vladimir spoke, Edward nodded.

"As long as you don't fuck around with Russia, Russia doesn't fuck around with you!" Both men laughed, but Snowden did pick up on Putin's ice cold eyes, he was a man that meant business and this was definatly not the guy to fuck with.

Many servings of "lunch" followed and it was rumored the visit extended into "the little hours of the cold Moscow winternight" with both men reminiscing about the horrible things America has done and was actively trying to hide from the general public.

The point was that Airbnb applies its own standards which may or may not be better.

Except Airbnb's standards are always to suppress anything negative at all costs. They delete bad reviews, they cover up bad situations, and refuse to pay out for hosting disasters until either media or law gets involved.

On the other hand, if Airbnb (or a company like it) realized that one of its listed properties had experienced a fire or a violent crime, or had provided breakfast that made the tenant rush to the hospital, then the company would immediately respond by taking the property off the website to investigate further. If it realized, say, that orange juice made by a certain company was giving people food poisoning, Airbnb might alert all of its landlords in the affected region and not steer customers to those rooms until it was satisfied that the problem had been addressed.

This is completely wrong, as has been shown in practice time and time again.

Nobody gives a shit about "safety" issues - that's a total red herring. There are two big ones: insurance and slumlords. The first is universal - what happens when a guest comes and destroys a place? Airbnb has their million-dollar insurance policy, but in practice, it's extremely difficult to get anything out of them. Their default response is to deny, even (especially?) in the massive damage cases, at which point the host's only real recourse is to hope for media attention... filing a police report for damages helps somewhat, but it's mostly the media spotlight that greases the wheels.
The second issue is only in select markets, but we're definitely seeing it in New York. Building landlords are reserving apartments for Airbnb only - it's cheaper than a hotel, but way more than what they'd get out of a long-term tenant. NYC has a pretty big affordable housing shortage anyway, and this certainly doesn't help matters.
